align.prompt: Ablation baseline: LLM straighten for as-twn-kaohsiung-shape-rect variant orig-llm-working2grid-sonnet5.

transcript.note: Round1: three off-alignment leaf/near-leaf moves. Vertex1 (deg1 endpoint) col 3->5 to match hub9's column, turning the 1-9 edge into pure V. Vertex5 (deg2, row locked at 8 via H edge to hub9) col 3->4 to match hub3's column (moving hub3 itself would collide with vertex15 at (3,5), so moved the non-hub side instead), turning 5-3 into pure V. Vertex2 (deg1 endpoint) row 0->2 to match hub7's row (hub7 is locked both row+col so left untouched), turning 7-2 into pure H. Left the two already-45-degree diagonals (8-3, 8-7) alone: both endpoints of each are locked/blocked by collisions (target cells occupied by vertex15 and vertex17 respectively), so no short move upgrades them without a collision.

Round2: vertex8 is a degree-4 hub locked in row (4) by two H edges (4-8, 8-17) but free in column. Moving its column 3->4 makes the 8-3 edge pure V (col8 now matches col3=4, which is itself locked both ways by 5-3's V edge and 15-3/0-3's H edges, so 3 could not move). This necessarily breaks the 8-7 edge's existing 45-degree diagonal (dx changes from 2 to 1, no longer |dx|=|dy|) since that diagonal only existed at col8=3; verified via winding check that 8's neighbour bearing order (17,3,4,7 CCW) is preserved by the move, so it should not be rejected on rule 4. Net effect: +1 true H/V (19->20) at the cost of one diagonal alignment (21->20 on the H/V+45 combined count), which is worth it since H/V is the primary criterion.
